items.headline: 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign escalates: Huang discusses Nvidia comeback with allies as reinstatement petition tops 155,000
items.summary: The FT/Bloomberg reported Sunday Nov 15 that Jensen Huang has discussed a possible return as Nvidia CEO with confidants, as Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Garry Tan and investors Brad Gerstner (Altimeter) and Gavin Baker (Atreides) publicly pressed the board to keep a path open for his reinstatement; a public petition passed 155,000 signatures. Nvidia's board has not responded publicly and says it is still engaging a search firm while its independent investigation into Huang's conduct continues.
items.actionable: A genuine comeback path (vs. a clean leadership vacuum) is a new variable for AI/semis sentiment -- it cuts both ways for SMIC/HSTech, so don't treat Monday's open as a one-way bearish continuation; watch for any board statement during Asia hours.

items.headline: Reuters finds $3.2B of China AI projects still spec'ing restricted Nvidia chips, contradicting Huang's 'zero China' claims
items.summary: A Reuters review of 150+ Chinese procurement notices, published the day before Huang's resignation, found roughly $3.2B in Chinese AI data-center projects specifying Nvidia's export-restricted H100/H200/H800 chips, versus IDC estimates Nvidia still held ~34% of Chinese AI-accelerator shipments in H1 2026 -- despite Huang telling investors China's contribution was effectively zero. The figure covers whole-project cost (not just chip sales) and spans operating, under-construction and planned sites.
items.actionable: Keeps the chip-export-enforcement scandal (and the Lutnick Dec 3/10 Senate hearings) alive as a live overhang on Chinese AI-chip access generally -- relevant context for SMIC (0981.HK) even though it isn't the direct subject.

items.headline: Tencent faces fresh US curbs threat on remote AI-chip access days before its Nov 18 earnings
items.summary: Reports that Washington is preparing tighter restrictions on Chinese firms' remote (cloud-based) access to advanced US AI chips hit Tencent shares (-2%) and put a specific policy cloud over its Q3 results due Wednesday Nov 18, since Tencent's AI roadmap leans partly on overseas compute access rather than only on-shore chips. SMIC and Hua Hong bucked the move, rallying on the same news as domestic-chip beneficiaries.
items.actionable: Direct, idiosyncratic read-through for Tencent (0700.HK) ahead of its Wednesday print -- expect the stock to trade on compute-access-risk headlines into earnings rather than on fundamentals alone; SMIC's inverse reaction is a partial domestic-chip hedge already visible in the complex.

items.headline: December Fed hike odds climb to ~95% through the weekend; Waller's 50bp trial balloon still in play
items.summary: CME FedWatch-implied odds of a December 25bp hike rose from ~72% a week ago to ~88.8% Friday and were tracked near 95% by Sunday Nov 15 (with a residual ~5% chance of 50bp), as hot October CPI/PPI prints and hawkish Fed commentary (including Governor Waller's floated 50bp option) continued to firm up through the weekend ahead of the Dec 9 FOMC and the Nov 25 PCE report.
items.actionable: A December hike is now priced as close to a certainty, not just a probability -- this is the dominant headwind for the silver/miner sleeve into Dec 9, and the Nov 25 PCE print is now the key swing event to watch before adding risk.

items.headline: Bitcoin enters the week at a 3-month low (~$64,800) on 7 straight days of ETF outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $64,800-65,400 on Sunday Nov 15, down roughly 14% over seven days and entering the week of Nov 16-22 at its lowest level in three months; US spot BTC ETFs logged roughly $1.91B of cumulative outflows over seven consecutive sessions. The slide continues to track the hawkish December-hike repricing plus lingering Nvidia/Huang-driven risk aversion rather than any crypto-specific catalyst.
items.actionable: Confirms the weekend risk-off mood carries into Monday's Asia open with no sign of stabilization -- expect continued correlated pressure on HK tech and no 'flight to metals' bid this cycle, since silver is still trading like a rate-sensitive risk asset, not a safe haven.

items.headline: Silver hits a one-year low (~$48.65, -2.6%) Friday while gold holds near $3,884 into the weekend
items.summary: COMEX silver settled at $48.65 on Friday Nov 13 (-2.6% on the day), its weakest level in a year, and was still quoted around $48.5-49.5 through the weekend; gold was far more resilient, holding near $3,884/oz with only marginal weekend moves. The divergence underscores that the rate-hike repricing is hitting silver's industrial/risk-asset character harder than gold's safe-haven bid.
items.actionable: The gold/silver divergence (gold firm, silver at a 1-year low) is itself a signal -- the silver/miner sleeve is currently trading on rate fear, not on the still-intact 46.3Moz deficit thesis; don't average down mechanically until the Dec 9 FOMC uncertainty resolves.

items.headline: Taiwan logs 10 PLA aircraft, 8 warships, 3 coast-guard vessels Fri-Sat; 184 aircraft/141 ship sorties so far this month
items.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense tracked 10 Chinese military aircraft, 8 naval vessels and 3 official ships in the 24 hours to Saturday Nov 14, four of which crossed the Strait median line; Defense Minister Wellington Koo described a broader 'area denial' drill in the western Pacific involving a carrier group. Taiwan has now logged 184 PLA aircraft and 141 ship sorties cumulatively in November, continuing what Taipei calls deliberate pressure timed ahead of the Nov 18-19 Shenzhen APEC summit.
items.actionable: The Strait tail-risk overhang on HK tech remains elevated but contained; the key swing factor is now the Nov 19 Trump-Xi meeting at APEC, not the drills themselves -- no new action warranted ahead of that.

items.headline: Unprecedented Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral confirmed for Nov 19 at Shenzhen APEC; AI and nuclear arms on the agenda
items.summary: The White House and Kremlin confirmed Trump will meet Xi bilaterally Thursday Nov 19 at the Shenzhen APEC summit (Nov 18-19), followed by an unprecedented Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral the same day covering nuclear-arms reduction, AI and broader trade -- the same framework under which China's rare-earth export-control pause (now extended to Jan 10, 2027) and US tariff exclusions on 178 Chinese goods were negotiated.
items.actionable: This is the single biggest scheduled catalyst of the next week for both the rare-earth watchlist (any trade-truce extension or breakdown moves MP/Lynas) and HK tech sentiment -- avoid large directional bets into Nov 18-19 given the binary-ish outcome risk.

items.headline: Houthi-Saudi escalation continues into the weekend: Yanbu/Aramco/pipeline strikes, then Yemeni forces pull back near Bab al-Mandab
items.summary: Following Thursday's Houthi drone/missile strikes on the Saudi East-West pipeline pumping station, the Yanbu oil facility and an Aramco building in Riyadh (two drones intercepted by the Saudi-led coalition), southern Yemeni government-aligned forces withdrew from positions near the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday Nov 15, raising the risk of further contested control over that chokepoint; the UN Security Council separately extended Yemen sanctions this week.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio holding, but a genuine Red Sea chokepoint/Saudi-infrastructure risk escalating (not de-escalating) over the weekend is part of the geopolitical risk premium propping up gold even as silver sells off on rates -- context for the precious-metals sleeve.

items.headline: China extends rare-earth export-control suspension to January 10, 2027; dysprosium/terbium/yttrium curbs stay in force
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce extended by two months (to Jan 10, 2027) the pause on the broader rare-earth/battery export controls, part of the trade-truce framework with Washington now feeding into the Nov 18-19 Shenzhen APEC summit. Licensing requirements on dysprosium, terbium and yttrium remain explicitly intact, with dysprosium oxide prices outside China still up ~242% year-to-date to around $4,100/kg.
items.actionable: Removes the near-term tail risk of a sudden re-imposition of the widest controls, but heavy-REE curbs staying intact keeps a structural price floor under MP/Lynas magnet-supply-chain names; the Jan 10, 2027 date and the Nov 18-19 Trump-Xi meeting are the next catalysts.

items.headline: MP Materials clears GM magnet-qualification milestone; three insiders bought $3.35M on Form 4
items.summary: MP Materials completed General Motors magnet qualification -- a concrete step toward becoming a vertically integrated US magnet supplier -- and is reportedly targeting Apple as a next customer, following a Q3 revenue beat (+176% y/y to $147.7M). A director, the COO and the CFO bought a combined ~$3.35M of stock on Nov 10-11, verified against SEC Form 4 filings; the stock traded around $37-40 through Nov 14.
items.actionable: A tangible commercial proof point plus a genuine three-insider buying cluster strengthens the ex-China magnet thesis underpinning the MP position on the rare-earth watchlist.

items.headline: Hang Seng tumbles 1.55% to 23,637.60, HSTech -3%, Alibaba -7% on Nvidia-scandal fallout
items.summary: Friday's HK close saw the Hang Seng Index fall 370.95 points (1.55%) and the Hang Seng Tech Index drop 3.02%, extending a three-session losing streak. Alibaba fell 7% (its worst day since August) and Hua Hong Semiconductor fell 6.1% as investors priced in fallout from the Nvidia CEO scandal, while PetroChina (+2.79%) bucked the trend on firmer oil.
items.actionable: Direct read-through for Tencent (0700.HK) and the HSTech complex into Monday's open -- combined with the weekend's further BTC deleveraging and the Huang-comeback uncertainty, the base case remains a weak-to-mixed Asia tech open rather than a clean bounce.

items.headline: STI falls ~1% to 5,231.84 Friday on regional Nvidia jitters, DBS leading declines; OCBC's Q3 beat vs DBS/UOB misses still the latest SG-bank read
items.summary: The Straits Times Index closed down 50.86 points (-0.96%) at 5,231.84 on Friday Nov 13, tracking the regional tech-led selloff, with DBS among the biggest drags. The most recent bank-specific fundamentals remain OCBC's Q3 net profit +3% y/y to S$2.04B (beat, guidance raised) against DBS's ~5% y/y profit decline (miss) on weaker trading income, with no fresher SG-bank data released over the weekend.
items.actionable: OCBC's guidance raise supports relative strength within the SGX bank sleeve; DBS's miss plus its leading role in Friday's index decline argues for keeping DBS exposure sized smaller than OCBC into the hawkish-Fed-driven volatility expected this week.
